title: The Historian's Son: Cheltenham, the Unit, the Rostrum, and the Long Premiership
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Tel Aviv, the birth of the second son
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: A second son is born to Benzion Netanyahu and Tzila Segal. The state is seventeen months old. The father is a historian of the Spanish Inquisition and was secretary to Vladimir Jabotinsky, and his scholarship is one argument pressed for sixty years: that the expulsion of the Jews from Spain was racial before it was religious, that hatred does not negotiate, that assurances from the gentile world are worth nothing. Between an older brother called Yonatan and a younger called Iddo, the boy grows up inside that argument as inside a house.
suggested_refs: Benzion Netanyahu's The Origins of the Inquisition in Fifteenth Century Spain, the father's lifelong argument
sources: Anshel Pfeffer, Bibi: The Turbulent Life and Times of Benjamin Netanyahu (2018)

stops.name: Jerusalem, the canonical stone above the schoolroom
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the sources give the city and the school and no address
stops.campa: The family lives in Jerusalem through the early childhood and the boy attends the Henrietta Szold Elementary School. No reachable source names a neighbourhood, so the atlas pins him where it pins every Jerusalem traveler, on the platform at 31.778, 35.2354 that solomon raises a temple on, that maimonides prays on in 1165 and keeps as a private annual festival for the rest of his life. The child walks beneath it without remark. The man will spend three decades declaring its sovereignty non-negotiable.
suggested_refs: The canonical Jerusalem coordinate of the atlas, inherited byte-identical across sixteen travelers

stops.name: Jerusalem, Gymnasia Leyada and the schooling cut short
stops.date_confidence: inferred year; the pool's geography lens dates this school to 1967-1968, after Cheltenham, which inverts the chronology
stops.campa: He is enrolled at the Hebrew University Secondary School, Gymnasia Leyada, beside the Givat Ram campus, and does not graduate from it: the family's move to the United States takes him out mid-course. The same university will one day give an honorary doctorate to edward_witten, whose family spent an unlocated year in Israel in this decade. Netanyahu never studies there. He will govern the state that funds it, and will be schooled instead in a Pennsylvania suburb, in a language that is not his mother's.
suggested_refs: The Givat Ram campus of the Hebrew University, beside the school he left without a diploma

stops.name: Wyncote, Cheltenham High School and the American voice
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Benzion has taught at Dropsie College in Philadelphia since 1957; in 1963 the family follows him and the boy enters Cheltenham High School on Rices Mill Road. He graduates with the class of 1967 and is later placed in the school's hall of fame. Pennsylvania gives him an unaccented American English, learned young enough to be native. For fifty years it will make him the most legible Israeli in the world to a television audience that has never been to Israel, and the first one they believe.
suggested_refs: Cheltenham High School yearbook, class of 1967

stops.name: Tel Aviv, enlistment in the Unit
stops.date_confidence: attested year, inferred month; no reachable source names the unit's base, so the pin marks the Kirya defence compound
stops.campa: He returns to Israel from Pennsylvania and enlists, and is selected for Sayeret Matkal, the General Staff Reconnaissance Unit, which takes its men by test rather than by application. His brother Yonatan is already a soldier. Where the unit trains and from what base it flies, the reachable sources do not say, so the atlas pins the enlistment to the Kirya compound in Tel Aviv and admits the substitution. He will serve five years and finish a captain, and the five years will be quoted for the rest of his life.
suggested_refs: The Sayeret Matkal selection process, gibush, of the late 1960s

stops.name: Karameh, the first battle
stops.date_confidence: attested month; the day follows the standard dating of the battle
stops.campa: In March the army crosses the Jordan against the Fatah base at Karameh and finds the Jordanian army waiting beside it. Netanyahu fights there. Israel takes the camp and withdraws with dead and abandoned vehicles behind it, and Fatah takes the day as its founding victory and names itself for the town. Two nations write the same afternoon in opposite directions. The young soldier of Sayeret Matkal is inside the first draft of a story that will still be running when he is prime minister for the third time.
suggested_refs: Contemporary IDF accounts of the Karameh raid, 21 March 1968

stops.name: Lod Airport, the Sabena aircraft on the tarmac
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Black September takes Sabena Flight 571 on 8 May and puts it down at Lod. The next day sixteen commandos in white mechanics' overalls walk out to the aircraft under Ehud Barak's command and storm it in ninety seconds. Netanyahu is wounded, and the sources will not agree how. His own biography says he was shot in the shoulder. The article on the flight says the commando Marko Ashkenazi fired by accident while striking the hijacker Theresa Halsa, and the round went through her and into Netanyahu's arm. Both accounts stand; the atlas does not choose.
suggested_refs: Operation Isotope, 9 May 1972, and the photographs of the white overalls

stops.name: Tel Aviv, the discharge, the first wife, and a deportation
stops.date_confidence: attested year, inferred month
stops.campa: He is discharged with the rank of seren, captain, and marries Miriam Weizmann, and by the end of the year he is on a plane to Massachusetts. In Jerusalem that same year the Supreme Court hears meyer_lansky, who has flown to Israel and petitioned for citizenship under the Law of Return, and rules against him, and Israel deports the old man back toward the United States he came from. The two men pass each other in opposite directions across the same border, neither aware of the other, one leaving to study and one leaving under escort.
suggested_refs: The 1972 Israeli Supreme Court ruling on Meyer Lansky and the Law of Return

stops.name: Cambridge, the student who calls himself Ben Nitay
stops.date_confidence: attested period, inferred month of arrival
stops.campa: He enrols at MIT under the name Ben Nitay, which is easier in an American mouth, and takes a bachelor's degree in architecture in February 1975 and a master's from the Sloan School in 1976. He is a foreign student with a war behind him among undergraduates who have none, and he is faster than the course: four years for two degrees. The name does the work the accent does. He is understood by Americans a decade before any Israeli electorate has heard of him. He does not go home when the degrees are finished.
suggested_refs: MIT registrar records under the name Ben Nitay, 1972-1976
sources: MIT alumni records, via the research pool

stops.name: The Chinese Farm, recalled to the Canal
stops.date_confidence: attested month; the pool placed this seventeen kilometres north of the battlefield
stops.campa: In October the war comes and he is on a plane the other way, out of Cambridge and back into uniform, and he fights on the Egyptian front near the irrigation works the army calls the Chinese Farm, six kilometres south of the crossing at Deversoir. The pool that reached this atlas had him discharged in October 1973 rather than recalled in it, and had the battlefield seventeen kilometres north of where the dead lie. Both are corrected here. He goes back to Massachusetts and finishes the architecture degree.
suggested_refs: The Chinese Farm battlefield east of the Suez Canal, north of the Great Bitter Lake

stops.name: Entebbe, the brother who does not come back
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Four Hercules aircraft land in the dark at an airport two and a half thousand miles from Israel and Yonatan Netanyahu leads the ground force to the old terminal. The hostages are taken out. He is not. He is the only Israeli soldier killed, and the operation is named for him afterward, and the younger brother in Boston learns of it by telephone. Benjamin Netanyahu is not at Entebbe and never claims to be. Everything he does in public for the next forty-five years is dated, by him and by his opponents alike, from this night.
suggested_refs: Operation Thunderbolt, renamed Operation Yonatan after the raid
sources: Israeli government and IDF accounts of Operation Entebbe

stops.name: Boston, the consultant at the firm
stops.date_confidence: attested period, inferred month
stops.campa: With the Sloan degree he goes to the Boston Consulting Group as an economic consultant, where a young Mitt Romney works two desks away. He stays two years. The method he learns here, the balance sheet read as an argument, the state costed like a business, is the method he will bring to the Israeli finance ministry in 2003 and use to cut taxes, welfare and public payrolls at once. The Entebbe telephone call has already happened; the consulting years run beside a grief that has not yet found its public form.
suggested_refs: Boston Consulting Group alumni accounts of the 1976-1978 intake

stops.name: Jerusalem, the Jonathan Institute
stops.date_confidence: attested year; the pool's chronology lens dates the founding to 1978 and its geography lens to 1979, and the two are not reconciled
stops.campa: He founds an institute in his brother's name to study international terrorism and convenes its first conference in Jerusalem in July, and a second in Washington in June 1984. The conferences do something that outlives them: they gather hijacking, bombing and insurgency from four continents and name them one subject, with one vocabulary, addressed to Western governments in English. The institute is a memorial that functions as a career. He is twenty-nine, has held no office, and has just built himself a rostrum.
suggested_refs: Proceedings of the Jerusalem Conference on International Terrorism, July 1979

stops.name: Washington, deputy chief of mission
stops.date_confidence: attested year, inferred month
stops.campa: Moshe Arens brings him to the chancery on International Drive as deputy chief of mission, and within months Israel is in Lebanon and the embassy needs a voice that American networks will put on air without subtitles. He has that voice. He married Fleur Cates the year before. He has never stood for election in Israel. In Washington he becomes the most quotable Israeli in the United States, and he goes home years later carrying an American constituency into Israeli politics as a domestic asset.
suggested_refs: The Israeli chancery at 3514 International Drive NW, occupied since December 1980

stops.name: New York, the permanent mission at 800 Second Avenue
stops.date_confidence: attested year, inferred month
stops.campa: At thirty-four he is made Israel's permanent representative to the United Nations, the seventh to hold the post, and takes an office six blocks from the building he will spend four years arguing inside. He is not a career diplomat and does not behave like one. He treats the General Assembly as a broadcast studio with hostile programming, and he answers in the language of the audience beyond the chamber rather than the delegates in it. He holds the post until 1988, and leaves it to run for the Knesset.
suggested_refs: The Permanent Mission of Israel at 800 Second Avenue, New York
sources: Wikipedia, 'Permanent Mission of Israel to the United Nations'

stops.name: The General Assembly, the ambassador at the rostrum
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the ambassadorship is attested for 1984-1988, this stop stands for the whole tenure
stops.campa: For four years he speaks for Israel from this rostrum while, out of the frame, an arms channel to Iran runs through Tel Aviv: oliver_north flies repeatedly to meet Amiram Nir, counterterrorism adviser to Israel's prime minister, and adnan_khashoggi is said to bridge the financing through the same city, a routing his own file flags as reconstruction. Netanyahu is the state's English voice through the years the channel operates. No reachable source places him in it. The atlas records the overlap and not a connection.
suggested_refs: The Tower Commission report on the Israeli leg of the Iran arms channel, 1985-1986

stops.name: The Knesset, the member from nowhere
stops.date_confidence: attested year and election, inferred day
stops.campa: He comes home, joins Likud, and is elected to the twelfth Knesset with no party apprenticeship, no army generalship and no kibbutz behind him, on the strength of a face the country has watched on foreign television. He is made deputy foreign minister. In November of the following year the Jerusalem Post reports him recommending large-scale expulsions, a remark he afterward says applied only to inciters, and whose scope the record leaves genuinely unsettled. The line is quoted against him for thirty-five years.
stops.quote: I still believe that there are opportunities to expel many people.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Netanyahu, Jerusalem Post, November 1989. Verified only through the editorial discussion at en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Talk:Benjamin_Netanyahu, not against the original; the sentence does not appear in the live Wikiquote article, and editors there record its scope as ambiguous. The pool's attribution to Hotam magazine is a separate and unverified text.
suggested_refs: Jerusalem Post, November 1989, 'NETANYAHU RECOMMENDS LARGE-SCALE EXPULSIONS'
sources: Jerusalem Post, November 1989, via the editorial discussion at Wikiquote Talk:Benjamin Netanyahu

stops.name: Madrid, the delegation, and a grave on the Mount of Olives
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He sits in the Israeli delegation at the Madrid Conference as deputy foreign minister, in the first room where Israel, Syria, Jordan and the Palestinians are seated together. He marries Sara Ben-Artzi the same year. Eleven days after Madrid opens, robert_maxwell is buried on the Mount of Olives at a state funeral: Prime Minister Shamir attends, President Herzog eulogizes, heads of the intelligence services stand at the graveside, and ghislaine_maxwell, twenty-nine, stands with them. Netanyahu is two years from leading that state's largest party.
suggested_refs: The Madrid Conference, 30 October 1991
The Mount of Olives state funeral of Robert Maxwell, 10 November 1991

stops.name: Tel Aviv, the Likud chairmanship
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: At Metzudat Ze'ev he takes the party from the generation that founded it, defeating Benny Begin, son of Menachem, and David Levy, who had spent thirty years in its machinery. He is forty-three and has been in the Knesset five years. Likud is out of power and the Oslo process is about to be signed on a White House lawn without it. He becomes leader of the opposition to an agreement he intends to survive rather than to reverse, and begins the campaign against it in Hebrew at home and in English abroad.
suggested_refs: Metzudat Ze'ev, the Likud headquarters on Rehov Jabotinsky, Tel Aviv

stops.name: Jerusalem, sworn in as prime minister
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Seven months after Rabin is shot, Israel votes for a prime minister directly for the first time, and on 29 May Netanyahu takes it from Shimon Peres by less than a percentage point, a margin thinner than the count of spoiled ballots. On 18 June he is sworn in: the youngest prime minister in the state's history and the first born inside it. The man who learned to be understood in Pennsylvania and was elected on television now has the office, and no experience of governing anything larger than an embassy press section.
suggested_refs: The 1996 direct prime-ministerial ballot, the only one Israel held twice

stops.name: The Erez crossing, the first meeting with Arafat
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He has spent three years arguing that Oslo endangers the state, and in September he stands at the Erez crossing and shakes Yasser Arafat's hand because the office he now holds inherits the agreement whether he wants it or not. The handshake is photographed, and his own right uses the photograph against him within the day. He was elected to stop the process. On his first substantive day in office he is administering it, slowly, and paying for it at once on both flanks.
suggested_refs: Press photographs of the Erez handshake, 4 September 1996

stops.name: The Western Wall tunnel, the exit that opens onto riots
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Three weeks after Erez his government opens a new exit from the Hasmonean tunnel into the Muslim Quarter, an archaeological convenience in a city where nothing under the Temple Mount is archaeological. Riots run for days across the West Bank and Gaza; Israeli soldiers and Palestinian police shoot at each other for the first time since Oslo was signed; the dead run into the scores. He does not close the exit, and it is still the way visitors leave the tunnel thirty years later.
suggested_refs: The Hasmonean tunnel exit into the Via Dolorosa, opened 24 September 1996
sources: contemporary AP and Reuters reporting, September 1996

stops.name: Hebron, the protocol at the Cave of the Patriarchs
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool's chronology lens gives 14 January and its geography lens 15 January for the same event, and neither is the signing date
stops.campa: Israeli forces withdraw from four fifths of Hebron and stay in the fifth that holds the Cave of the Patriarchs and the settlers around it. Netanyahu and Arafat conclude the deal in the small hours of 15 January; the Knesset approves it on the 16th, eighty-seven to seventeen, and redeployment starts that day; on the 17th the document is signed, not by Netanyahu, but by General Dan Shomron for Israel and Saeb Erekat for the Palestinians. Both lenses of the research pool put his name on it. His name is not on it.
suggested_refs: The Hebron Protocol, signed 17 January 1997 by Dan Shomron and Saeb Erekat

stops.name: Amman, the antidote
stops.date_confidence: attested for the operation and the antidote; the pool's claim of a Netanyahu meeting with King Hussein at the palace is unsupported and is marked reconstruction
stops.campa: Mossad agents on Canadian passports put poison into Khaled Mashal's ear on an Amman street and are caught. King Hussein, who has a peace treaty with Israel three years old, demands the antidote or the treaty. Netanyahu consents and the Mossad chief Danny Yatom flies to Jordan carrying it, and Israel releases Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, the founder of Hamas, from prison as the price of the mess. The pool has Netanyahu himself at the royal palace over this. No reachable source puts him there. Yatom went.
suggested_refs: The Canadian passports used in the Mashal operation, and the diplomatic rupture with Ottawa

stops.name: Washington, the Wye River Memorandum signed at the White House
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool located the signing at the Wye River conference centre, which is where the talks were held and not where the document was signed
stops.campa: Nine days of negotiation at the Aspen Institute centres near Wye Mills in Maryland, with bill_clinton walking between two men who will not sit in a room together, produce a memorandum on further withdrawal in the West Bank. It is signed on 23 October at the White House, Clinton witnessing, not in Maryland. The Knesset approves it on 17 November. His own coalition begins to come apart over it within weeks; the government that was elected to stop the process falls for having continued it.
suggested_refs: The Wye River Memorandum, signed at the White House, 23 October 1998

stops.name: Tel Aviv, the election lost to Barak
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool's chronology lens gives 6 July 1999, which is the date Barak formed a government and not the date of the vote
stops.campa: Ehud Barak, who commanded the assault on the Sabena aircraft twenty-seven years earlier and had this man under his orders on the tarmac, takes fifty-six per cent to his forty-four. Netanyahu resigns the Likud leadership the same night and leaves the Knesset. The formal end of the term comes on 6 July when Barak forms the twenty-eighth government, and the research pool confuses that date with the defeat. He is forty-nine, finished by every account written that summer, and out of politics for two years.
suggested_refs: The 17 May 1999 direct ballot: Barak 1,791,020 votes, Netanyahu 1,402,474

stops.name: Ofra, the recording
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the tape is real and widely reported, but the circulating English wording could not be checked against a primary transcript in this pass
stops.campa: Out of office, he sits in a settlement north-east of Ramallah talking to a family whose son died in an attack, and a camera runs that he appears to forget. He explains how he emptied Oslo without breaking it, by insisting on Israel's own definition of the military zones. The tape surfaces in Israeli media nine years later, when he is prime minister again. The Hebrew is not in dispute. The English translation in circulation could not be checked against a primary transcript here, and the quote is carried on that footing.
stops.quote: I know what America is. America is a thing you can move very easily, move it in the right direction.
stops.quote_source: Netanyahu to settlers at Ofra, 2001, Hebrew original; English wording as circulated by Israeli and international press in 2010. Not verified against a primary transcript in this research pass; Guardian and Haaretz pages were unreachable.
suggested_refs: The 2001 Ofra recording, broadcast by Israeli television in 2010
sources: Widely reported transcript of the 2001 Ofra recording, circulated by Israeli and international press in 2010

stops.name: The Capitol, testimony for the invasion of Iraq
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction in the research pool's own tagging; the testimony is widely reported but was not verified against the committee record here
stops.campa: A private citizen with no office is called before the House Government Reform Committee and tells it that removing saddam_hussein will have enormous positive reverberations across the region. The Osirak reactor that Iraq built with French help was destroyed by Israeli aircraft in 1981, three years before he took the United Nations post and began warning the West about hostile states with reactors. The man in Baghdad is stamping Babylon's bricks with his own name in the manner of Nebuchadnezzar. Six months later the invasion begins.
suggested_refs: The record of the House Government Reform Committee hearing, 12 September 2002

stops.name: Jerusalem, the finance ministry
stops.date_confidence: attested year, inferred month
stops.campa: Sharon puts him at the treasury and he does there what he could not do as prime minister: he changes the country. Tax rates fall, state companies are sold, welfare payments and public payrolls are cut, and the shekel is turned toward the open market. Israeli growth follows and Israeli inequality follows too, and both are still argued over twenty years later. The Boston Consulting Group method, the state read as a balance sheet, is applied to a nation in the third year of the second intifada, with tourism gone and the shekel under pressure.
suggested_refs: The 2003 Israeli economic recovery plan and the sale of state holdings

stops.name: Jerusalem, the resignation over disengagement
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: As the last preparations are made to remove every soldier and settler from Gaza, he resigns from the cabinet rather than sign for it, and says so in the language of a man addressing a party rather than a government. Sharon leaves Likud and founds Kadima; Netanyahu takes what is left of Likud in the primary of 20 December and leads it into the 2006 election, where it wins twelve seats out of a hundred and twenty. He has the party and the party is a wreck. He spends three years rebuilding it.
suggested_refs: The Gaza disengagement of August 2005 and the Likud primary of 20 December 2005

stops.name: The Knesset, the second government
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Likud finishes second to Kadima in February and he becomes prime minister anyway, because Peres designates him on 20 February as the man who can assemble sixty-one seats and Tzipi Livni cannot. Kadima has twenty-eight seats, Likud twenty-seven. The government is approved on 31 March. This is the beginning of the twelve unbroken years, the longest premiership Israel has had, and it begins in an arithmetic the losing side never stops calling a theft. He will use the same arithmetic four more times.
suggested_refs: The 2009 Knesset election and the coalition arithmetic of February 2009

stops.name: Ramat Gan, the Bar-Ilan speech
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Ten weeks into the second government he says the words his own base has never allowed: a Palestinian state, demilitarized, recognizing Israel as the Jewish nation state. The conditions are heavy enough that both sides read the speech as a concession and neither reads it as an offer. Seventy years earlier martin_buber taught at the Hebrew University and argued through Brit Shalom and Ihud for one binational country, and was buried in 1965 with the President of Israel at the grave. Likud descends from the opposite tradition entirely.
suggested_refs: The Bar-Ilan University address, 14 June 2009, official PMO transcript
sources: Israeli Prime Minister's Office, official transcript of the Bar-Ilan address

stops.name: Sharm el-Sheikh, the direct talks
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool also listed a September 1999 Sharm summit for him, which belongs to Ehud Barak
stops.campa: Mubarak hosts the last round of direct Israeli-Palestinian negotiation that anyone convenes at this level, and hillary_clinton shuttles between the rooms as she has shuttled to Jerusalem since 2009. The talks collapse within weeks, when the moratorium on settlement construction expires on 26 September and is not renewed. The research pool also placed him at Sharm in September 1999, at the signing of a memorandum that was Barak's, three months after Netanyahu had left office. That stop is dropped. This one holds.
suggested_refs: The September 2010 direct talks at Sharm el-Sheikh and Washington

stops.name: The General Assembly, the drawing of a bomb
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He returns to the chamber where he was ambassador twenty-four years earlier and holds up a cartoon of a bomb with a fuse, and draws a red line across it with a marker in front of the world's delegations. It is ridiculed for a week and remembered for a decade. In 1979 ayatollah_khomeini instituted Quds Day, calling the Muslim world into the streets each Ramadan over the same platform in Jerusalem that this atlas pins at 31.778, 35.2354. The two arguments have been running against each other since before he held any office.
stops.quote: Red lines don't lead to war; red lines prevent war.
stops.quote_source: Speech to the 67th United Nations General Assembly, 27 September 2012, transcript hosted on Wikisource
suggested_refs: The cartoon bomb diagram held up at the 67th General Assembly, 27 September 2012
sources: Speech to the 67th United Nations General Assembly, 27 September 2012, transcript hosted on Wikisource

stops.name: Beijing, the Great Hall of the People
stops.date_confidence: attested month, inferred day; the pool's coordinate landed in Tiananmen Square rather than in the building
stops.campa: He goes east to sell technology and buy patience, meets the Chinese leadership in the hall on the west side of the square, and comes home with agreements on water, agriculture and infrastructure. The visit is a hedge written in advance: a state that has depended on one guarantor since 1967 opening a second line to a power that votes against it at the United Nations without fail. Israeli firms follow. The Americans notice, and say so about the ports, and the hedging continues anyway for another decade.
suggested_refs: The May 2013 Israeli state visit to Beijing and the technology agreements signed

stops.name: The Capitol, the speech against the Iran deal
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: John Boehner invites him to address a joint meeting of Congress without telling the White House, and he comes and argues against a nuclear agreement the sitting American president is negotiating, from the American legislature's own floor, seven weeks before an Israeli election. Fifty-eight Democrats stay away. The speech does not stop the agreement, which is signed in July. It does something else: it makes the alliance a partisan question in Washington for the first time, and it stays one.
stops.quote: The greatest danger facing our world is the marriage of militant Islam with nuclear weapons.
stops.quote_source: Address to a Joint Meeting of the United States Congress, 3 March 2015; Israeli Prime Minister's Office transcript hosted on Wikisource
suggested_refs: The 3 March 2015 address to a joint meeting of Congress, and the fifty-eight empty seats
sources: Address to a Joint Meeting of the United States Congress, 3 March 2015, PMO transcript via Wikisource

stops.name: Jerusalem, the capital recognized
stops.date_confidence: attested month; the announcement is 6 December 2017 and the embassy moves the following May
stops.campa: An American president says the word capital aloud and moves the embassy, and the coordinate under the announcement is the one this atlas has used for solomon, for maimonides, for abraham, for bill_clinton putting a folded note into the stones in the 1990s, the single most reused pin in the whole collection, inherited byte-identical across sixteen travelers. Netanyahu has argued for this recognition since the United Nations years. What he gets is a word, a building on a hill, and no change at all in the status of the platform itself.
suggested_refs: The US recognition of December 2017 and the embassy move of May 2018

segments.name: The Record, the Trial, the War

stops.name: Beit Aghion, the record and the street outside it
stops.date_confidence: attested month for the record; the residence address is corrected from the pool, which placed it in Talbiya rather than Rehavia
stops.campa: In July he passes David Ben-Gurion's cumulative tenure and becomes the longest-serving prime minister the state has had. He passes it inside a house at 9 Smolenskin Street on the corner of Balfour, in Rehavia, which the research pool put in the wrong neighbourhood. Within a year the corner outside is the fixed address of a protest that runs for three years, first over the indictment and then over the courts, with his own face carried past the gate on placards reading crime minister.
suggested_refs: Beit Aghion, 9 Smolenskin Street, and the Balfour Street protest encampment
sources: contemporary reporting on the Balfour Street protests, 2020-2023

stops.name: Jerusalem, the defendant on Salah ad-Din Street
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool carried two different coordinates for this court and neither matched it
stops.campa: Indicted on 21 November 2019, he walks into the district court in East Jerusalem on 24 May 2020 as a sitting prime minister on trial: Case 1000 and Case 2000 for fraud and breach of trust, Case 4000 for those and bribery. He does not resign, because Israeli law does not require it of a prime minister. The trial runs for years alongside the office. Two lenses of the research pool put this building in two different places, both in the wrong half of the city, and the atlas corrects them both.
suggested_refs: The Jerusalem District Court on Salah ad-Din Street, and the indictment of 21 November 2019

stops.name: The White House, the Abraham Accords
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On the South Lawn he signs normalization with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, and Morocco and Sudan follow. It is the thing he wanted and could not get for twenty-five years: Arab recognition without a Palestinian settlement first, the sequence he always argued was the correct one, inverted in public. Nobody signs for the Palestinians and nobody is asked to. The atlas finds no confirmed personal visit by him to Manama and does not pin one, though Bahrain's name is on the document under his.
suggested_refs: The Abraham Accords Declaration, signed on the South Lawn, 15 September 2020

stops.name: The Knesset, out and back
stops.date_confidence: attested for the removal; the return is 29 December 2022 and both are carried in this stop
stops.campa: On 13 June 2021 Naftali Bennett assembles eight parties whose only agreement is his removal, and he goes to the opposition benches after twelve years. He is back on 29 December 2022 with the most right-wing coalition the state has formed, and inside three months it moves on the courts and half a million people are in the streets of Tel Aviv every Saturday night. In this same chamber in 2024 adi_shamir will be handed the Wolf Prize, one more ceremony falling inside a government he leads.
suggested_refs: The 2023 judicial overhaul legislation and the Kaplan Street demonstrations

stops.name: Jerusalem, the statement of the seventh of October
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: At dawn on a Saturday that is also a holiday, gunmen come through the Gaza fence in numbers nobody in the state believed possible, and by the time he speaks the country has taken the worst single day of killing in its history. He declares war from Jerusalem. The war that follows runs longer than any Israel has fought, and every judgement of him, at home and abroad, is written afterward from this morning. He is seventy-four and in his sixth term, and the security argument of his whole life has failed at its own border.
stops.quote: Dear citizens of Israel, This morning, on Shabbat and a holiday, Hamas invaded Israeli territory and murdered innocent citizens including children and the elderly.

stops.name: Southern Israel, the burned communities of the Gaza envelope

stops.campa: He walks through the kibbutzim along the fence with the soldiers and the reporters, past houses still standing open, and is heckled in some of them by people who want to know where the army was. The communities here voted against him for years. The war he is now conducting is fought within a few kilometres of these gardens, and the hostages taken from them are the subject on which his government is judged inside Israel, separately and more harshly than on anything the outside world charges him with.

stops.name: The Hague, the warrant
stops.date_confidence: attested; the research pool carried two different and equally wrong coordinates for this building
stops.campa: Pre-Trial Chamber I issues an arrest warrant for a sitting prime minister of Israel: the war crime of starvation as a method of warfare, the war crime of intentionally directing attacks against civilians, and the crimes against humanity of murder, persecution and other inhumane acts, for conduct from at least 8 October 2023 to at least 20 May 2024. Israel and the United States reject the court's jurisdiction over Israeli nationals outright. The warrant stands, contested and largely unenforced. That contest is not resolved here.

stops.campa: There is a private house on the coast north of Tel Aviv, the subject of state comptroller reports and years of argument about who paid for what in it, and the atlas can place it only to the town and says so. Here the standard form of this collection stops working. Every other traveler in it has a grave, a legend that grew after the grave, and a date that closed the file. This one is alive, in office, on trial in one court and charged in another, and the last stop is a gap that is stated as a gap.
